terms.d: Written instruction (living will or DPAHC) guiding care when individual is terminally ill, incapacitated, or unable to communicate wishes.
Tax-advantaged savings for individuals with disabilities (onset before age 46 as of 2026); no ISM penalty for food/shelter paid from the account; up to $100,000 excluded from SSI resource limit.
Activities of Daily Living — self-care tasks: bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transferring, continence.
Agent under a power of attorney (identical to "agent under POA").
Objective decision-making standard: what a reasonable person would do. Used when substituted judgment is unavailable.
Bank or brokerage account requiring court authorization for withdrawals; allows smaller or no bond.
Insurance requirement guaranteeing proper fiduciary performance; amount based on estate value.
Legal qualification and competency; ability to understand the nature and effects of one's acts.
Community Spouse Resource Allowance — assets the non-institutionalized spouse may retain when the other spouse qualifies for Medi-Cal SNF or HCBS coverage ($162,660 in 2026).
Disabled Adult Child — SSA benefits category for adult children with disabilities.
SSA process of attributing parents' or spouse's income/assets to an SSI-eligible individual (irrebuttable presumption).
Category of disorders with multiple cognitive deficits including memory impairment.

Severe, chronic disability manifested before age 18 under California's Lanterman Act (WIC §4512); substantial limitations in 3+ of 7 major life activities. (The federal DD Act uses age 22 — CA exam answer is 18.)
Do Not Resuscitate — order to not perform CPR. Does NOT mean "do not treat."
Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care — advance directive designating an agent for healthcare decisions; survives incapacity.
Judging other cultures as inferior to one's own.
Improper or illegal use of a person's funds, resources, or assets.

IRS Notice Concerning Fiduciary Relationship — filed when the relationship is created (and again at termination) so IRS notices reach the fiduciary. Distinct from Form 4810, the request for prompt assessment that shortens the IRS assessment window to 18 months.
Diagnostic tool measuring overall well-being and ability to function in multidimensional situations.
Person appointed by court to make an impartial inquiry and report.
Instrumental Activities of Daily Living — complex tasks: managing finances, shopping, cooking, housekeeping, using transportation.
In-Home Supportive Services — Medi-Cal program paying for in-home care; max 283 hours/month (severely impaired) or 195 hours (non-severely impaired).
Institute for Mental Disease — long-term locked facility for mentally ill; subcategory of SNF.
Agreement made with knowledge of risks, benefits, and alternatives.
In-Kind Support and Maintenance — SSI term for shelter provided to a beneficiary; triggers benefit reduction. Since 9/30/2024 only shelter (not food) counts.
Licensed fiduciaries must complete 15 hours of continuing education each year to renew — including at least 2 hours of ethics and/or cultural competency. A favorite exam question.
Assets readily convertible to cash: savings/checking accounts, CDs, money market and mutual funds. Real estate, collectibles, and stamps are NOT liquid.
Helping a person make their own decisions with assistance (advisors, tools, trusted supporters) instead of substituting a decision for them — a less restrictive alternative.
Setting placing the fewest limits on rights and freedoms while meeting the person's needs.
Court document evidencing appointment and authority; must be recently certified (within 60 days).
For adults with developmental disabilities; only specific powers granted by the court.
Lanterman-Petris-Short Act conservatorship for grave disability due to mental illness, severe substance use disorder, or co-occurring conditions (expanded by SB 43); only the county can petition.
Requirement in first-party SNTs that remaining trust funds reimburse Medicaid upon beneficiary's death.
Investment framework weighing risks and rewards across diversified holdings.
Legal document signed by guardian pledging to carry out obligations properly.
Legal principle allowing the state to determine what's in an individual's best interests.
Presumed Maximum Value — rebuttable cap for shelter ISM outside the VTR situation: one-third of FBR plus $20 ($351.33/month in 2026). Recipient can rebut by showing actual value is lower.
Court-appointed appraiser for estate assets.
Evaluate the portfolio as a whole; diversify; consider risk tolerance and constraints. Default standard under Probate Code §16046(a).
Older standard evaluating each investment individually for reasonableness.
Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (Assisted Living).
Nonprofit serving individuals with developmental disabilities under the Lanterman Act; no income/asset test; payer of last resort.
Person/entity named by a government agency to receive benefits on behalf of a beneficiary.
Doctrine that actions are determined by the person; free choice without external force.
Skilled Nursing Facility.
Person whose appointment becomes effective upon the initially appointed guardian's death, incapacity, resignation, or temporary absence.
Decision-making based on what the incapacitated person would have wanted, using their known prior wishes.

Value of One-Third Reduction — flat SSI reduction (one-third of FBR; $331.33/month in 2026) applying only when a recipient lives a full month in another's household, receives shelter without paying a pro-rata share, AND household members provide ALL meals. Anything less → PMV instead.

timelines.r: Advance notice (with copy of petition) required for a temporary conservatorship hearing
File the §2253 request after a temporary conservator makes an emergency move (Prob. Code §2254)
File the Care Plan after appointment — level of care is determined at appointment and included in it (SB 280, eff. 2025; replaced the old 60-day determination)
Letters of Conservatorship must be recently certified
Annual Statement filing deadline before license expiration
Earliest point fees may be requested after appointment
Reappraisal window for selling the conservatee's PERSONAL RESIDENCE (§2543(c)); other estate property uses a 1-year appraisal window (§10309)
Notice of sale must be published in a newspaper (no fixed window — publication simply precedes the sale; §10300)
IRS standard audit statute; Probate Code §16460 breach claims
IRS extended audit statute (omitted >25% gross income)
